definitions.gloss: to flare up, to burst into flames, to blaze up
definitions.explanation: For fire or flames to suddenly rise up intensely. Describes the dramatic moment when something catches fire or when flames grow in intensity.

definitions.gloss: to be inflamed, to burn with passion
definitions.explanation: For emotions such as anger, passion, or fighting spirit to surge intensely. A figurative extension of the fire imagery.

examples.japanese: {炎|ほのお}が{燃|も}え{上|あ}がった。
{風|かぜ}で{火|ひ}が{一気|いっき}に{燃|も}え{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: The fire flared up all at once in the wind.

examples.japanese: {乾燥|かんそう}した{落|お}ち{葉|ば}に{火|ひ}がつき、あっという{間|ま}に{燃|も}え{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: The dry fallen leaves caught fire and blazed up in an instant.

examples.japanese: {闘志|とうし}が{燃|も}え{上|あ}がる。
examples.english: My fighting spirit is fired up.

examples.japanese: {観客|かんきゃく}の{応援|おうえん}で{選手|せんしゅ}たちが{燃|も}え{上|あ}がった。
examples.english: The athletes were fired up by the cheering of the spectators.

examples.japanese: {不正|ふせい}に{対|たい}する{怒|いか}りが{国中|くにじゅう}で{燃|も}え{上|あ}がり、{大規模|だいきぼ}なデモに{発展|はってん}した。
examples.english: Anger against the injustice flared up across the country, developing into large-scale protests.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
Godan verb ({燃|も}え{上|あ}がる → {燃|も}え{上|あ}がります). A compound verb formed from {燃|も}える (to burn) + {上|あ}がる (to rise). Intransitive — there is no direct transitive counterpart.

The {上|あ}がる component adds the nuance of upward movement and sudden intensification, distinguishing this from the more neutral {燃|も}える.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {炎|ほのお}が{燃|も}え{上|あ}がる: flames flare up
- {闘志|とうし}が{燃|も}え{上|あ}がる: fighting spirit flares up
- {怒|いか}りが{燃|も}え{上|あ}がる: anger flares up
- {一気|いっき}に{燃|も}え{上|あ}がる: to blaze up all at once
